routes.label: Subtract two end pieces from a triangular prism

question:
In the rectangular parallelepiped shown, \(AB = 3,\) \(BC = 1,\) and \(CG = 2.\) Point \(M\) is the midpoint of \(FG.\) What is the volume of the rectangular pyramid with base \(BCHE\) and apex \(M?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_10B_Q10_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The inclined base makes the pyramid's height less convenient to find. Instead, split rectangle \(BCHE\) along diagonal \(BH\). This divides the pyramid into two tetrahedra, or triangular pyramids, \(M\text{-}BCH\) and \(M\text{-}BHE\). Each tetrahedron can use any of its triangular faces as a base, so choose faces lying in faces of the box. A pyramid's volume is one third of its base area times its perpendicular height.

For tetrahedron \(M\text{-}BCH\), use triangle \(MBC\) as the base. It lies in face \(BCGF\). Its base \(BC\) is \(1\), and its altitude is \(2\), because \(M\) lies on edge \(FG\), opposite and parallel to \(BC\). Thus its area is \(\frac12\cdot1\cdot2=1\). The perpendicular distance from \(H\) to this face is \(AB=3\), so
\[
V_1=\frac13\cdot1\cdot3=1.
\]
For tetrahedron \(M\text{-}BHE\), use triangle \(MHE\) in the top face as the base. Here \(HE=1\), and the altitude from \(M\) to \(HE\) is \(3\), the distance between opposite top edges \(FG\) and \(HE\). Its area is therefore \(\frac32\). The perpendicular distance from \(B\) to the top face is \(2\), giving
\[
V_2=\frac13\cdot\frac32\cdot2=1.
\]
The two tetrahedra fill the requested pyramid and share only their boundary face \(MBH\). Its volume is therefore \(1+1=\boxed{2}\) cubic units, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Cut the box along rectangle \(BCHE\), and consider the half containing edge \(FG\). This is a triangular prism with triangular ends \(BEF\) and \(CHG\). Each end is a right triangle with legs \(3\) and \(2\), so its area is \(3\). The prism's depth is \(BC=1\), giving volume
\[
V_{\text{prism}}=3\cdot1=3.
\]
Joining \(M\) to the diagonal rectangular face and to the two triangular ends divides this prism into the requested pyramid and tetrahedra \(M\text{-}BEF\) and \(M\text{-}CHG\). To justify this division, extend a ray from \(M\) through any interior point to its exit from the prism. The exit must lie on one of those three faces, since the other two faces lie in planes through \(M\). If the exit lies on the shared edge \(BE\) or \(CH\), the interior point lies on the common boundary triangle \(MBE\) or \(MCH\). Otherwise, the exit belongs to exactly one of the three faces. Thus the pieces fill the prism and have no overlapping interiors.

Because \(FG=BC=1\) and \(M\) is its midpoint, \(MF=MG=\frac12\). Edge \(FG\) is perpendicular to the triangular end faces, so each tetrahedron has base area \(3\) and perpendicular height \(\frac12\). Using one third of base area times height, each has volume
\[
\frac13\cdot3\cdot\frac12=\frac12.
\]
Subtracting these two end pieces gives the requested volume:
\[
3-\frac12-\frac12=\boxed{2}
\]
cubic units, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
